title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0576
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0576
Multiple Vulnerabilities in Whatsapp
Original Issue Date:November  26, 2026
Severity Rating: HIGH
Software Affected
WhatsApp for Android versions prior to 2.26.35.74 and 2.26.17.4
WhatsApp Business for Android versions prior to 2.26.23.70 and 2.26.17.4
WhatsApp Business for iOS  prior to v2.26.23.72
WhatsApp for iOS versions prior to 2.26.24.72 and 2.26.15.72
WhatsApp for Mac Desktop versions prior to v2.26.23.72
WhatsApp for Windows versions prior to v2.3000.1032164386.258709
Overview
Multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in WhatsApp which could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code, obtain sensitive information, or bypass security restrictions on the targeted system.
Target Audience:
Individuals and organizations using the affected WhatsApp, WhatsApp Business, and WhatsApp for Mac/Windows.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of arbitrary code execution, sensitive information disclosure, and bypassing security restrictions.
Impact Assessment:
Potential for compromise of affected systems, unauthorized access, and bypass of hardware root of trust.
Description
WhatsApp for Android, WhatsApp Business for Android, WhatsApp for iOS, WhatsApp for Mac Desktop, and WhatsApp for Windows are cross-platform communication applications developed by Meta, offering instant messaging, voice and video calling, and multimedia sharing.
These vulnerabilities exist in WhatsApp products due to attachment spoofing, SQL injection, improper certificate chain validation, incomplete validation of AI rich response messages and external ad-reply URLs. A remote attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by sending a specially crafted message, attachment, or URL to the targeted system.
Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code, obtain sensitive information, bypass security restrictions, or manipulate application data on the targeted system.
Solution
Apply appropriate updates as mentioned by the vendor:
https://www.whatsapp.com/security/advisories

title: CERT-In Vulnerability Note  CIVN-2026-0575
content:
CERT-In Vulnerability Note 
                                                                      CIVN-2026-0575
Multiple Vulnerabilities in Asus
Original Issue Date:November  26, 2026
Severity Rating: CRITICAL
Software Affected
ASUS Control Center Express versions prior to v1.7.29
ASUS Control Center Datacenter version 4.0.0.2 and earlier
ASUS Control Center Enterprise version 3.1.0.8 and earlier
ASUS Armoury Crate versions up to and including v6.7.2
Overview
Multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in ASUS products, which could allow a remote attacker to bypass authentication, forge authentication tokens, obtain administrative control, and gain elevated privileges on affected systems.
Target Audience:
All organizations, system administrators, and users utilizing the affected ASUS products.
Risk Assessment:
High risk of unauthorized administrative access to management consoles and potentially compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of managed systems.
Impact Assessment:
Potential for unauthorized administrative access, privilege escalation, authentication bypass, and compromise of managed devices.
Description
ASUS is a multinational computer hardware and electronics manufacturer that provides system management software, hardware configuration utilities, and enterprise IT management solutions.
Multiple vulnerabilities exist in ASUS products due to use of hard-coded cryptographic keys, incorrect authorization, missing authorization, and an untrusted search path. A remote attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities by forging authentication tokens, obtaining administrative privileges, creating unauthorized administrator accounts, changing administrator account passwords, bypassing authentication, or allow local low-privileged users to execute malicious libraries at a high integrity level.
Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow a remote attacker to bypass authentication, forge authentication tokens, obtain administrative control, and gain elevated privileges on affected systems.
Solution
Apply appropriate updates as mentioned in the ASUS Advisory:
https://www.asus.com/security-advisory#bulletins
